name: r01_four_holes_from_the_border
why: The most common case there is: four fixing holes 20 mm from the corners of a plate, and the plate widens. In the workshop those holes stay 20 mm from the edge -- that is what «20 from the corners» means.
intent_why: the holes are 20 mm from the edges: widening the plate from 120 to 180 they must stay at 20 mm, that is the two at the bottom stay at y = -40 and the two at the top go from +40 to +100: the plate grows ON ONE SIDE ONLY (entry E2), from Y -60..+60 to Y -60..+120.

after._why_these_numbers: until 25/9/2026 the expectation was [-70, -70, 70, 70], that is a plate growing symmetrically: E2 measured that it does not, and with that expectation the case could not have held even with the right anchor. Corrected when writing E18, before giving the anchor to hole_wizard.
after.tolerance_why: the cylinder axis is read from CylinderParams, which returns metres: the hundredth is rounding

_why_the_anchor: ENTRY E18, the last part. Up to library 0.118.0 the `build` gave the holes at absolute coordinates — an instruction nobody would give for «20 from the corners» — and the case stayed silent by construction. Now every position carries its anchor to the two nearby edges; the EXPECTATIONS are those from before (corrected on 25/9 because the plate grows on one side only). The old way is still proved by the twin `r01b_four_holes_stay_where_they_are`.
